none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: The objective is differentiable on all of ℝᵈ, has a globally L-Lipschitz gradient, and satisfies f(x₀) − inf f ≤ Δ. These conditions permit nonconvex objectives and do not require the infimum to be attained.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovSmoothNonconvex.lean, Space, spec.Instance, and the three objective conditions in spec.admissible

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: On call t the algorithm queries xₜ and receives only g(xₜ,Zₜ). Each call consumes the next state of a single hidden trajectory, including calls whose replies the algorithm discards. The public input is (d,L,Δ,σ,τ,ε,x₀). The objective, state space, transition kernel, stationary law, and gradient estimator are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply, and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean, Oracle.answer and executeWithTrace

distinctive_assumptions.label: markov_dependence
distinctive_assumptions.details: The chain starts from its invariant law π and evolves under a fixed kernel κ independently of the queries. For every state z and integer t ≥ 0, the total variation distance between κᵗ(z,·) and π is at most 2 exp(−t/τ), with τ ≥ 1.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/HeavyTailedMarkovSmoothAndConvex.lean, pathLaw and mixingDistance

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every fixed x, the jointly measurable estimator satisfies Eπ[g(x,Z)] = ∇f(x) and Eπ‖g(x,Z) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ². Both expectations use the stationary law. At an adaptive query, the conditional mean and variance given past replies may differ from these fixed-query moments.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovSmoothNonconvex.lean, measurability, integrability, mean, and centered second-moment clauses in spec.admissible

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Queries and outputs lie in Euclidean ℝᵈ, with d ≥ 2⁴⁰(1 + τLΔσ²/ε⁴)⁴.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The parameter regime requires L > 0, ε > 0, σ ≥ 4096ε, and LΔ ≥ 2²⁶ε². It allows both σ² < LΔ and σ² > LΔ.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns one measurable point X in ℝᵈ. The criterion uses the first power of the Euclidean norm of the true gradient at X. Any measurable output point is eligible.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: ‖∇f(X)‖ must be integrable and satisfy E‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε. The expectation is over the algorithm's private random seed and the stationary Markov trajectory, drawn independently.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/MarkovSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean, Convergence and its product measure

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The distinguishing feature is adaptive gradient access along one hidden, uniformly mixing Markov trajectory with only fixed-query stationary moment bounds. The dimension, noise, and initial-gap restrictions further specify the benchmark.
